conventions.convention: All quantitative vector bounds use the Euclidean norm and its induced operator norm. The bordered matrix stacks A above the row τᵀ; its angular factor is τᵀt.
The fold right nullvector v is unit, the left nullvector w need only be nonzero, X=v⊥, Y=ker(wᵀ), q=b/(wᵀb), and P=I−qwᵀ.
The fold parameter s is fixed by vᵀ(x(s)−x₀)=s; it is not asserted to be Euclidean arclength. With a=wᵀFλ and b=wᵀFxx[v,v], the curvature is λ″(0)=−b/a. The fold theorem assumes C³.

The normalized regular chart uses tᵀ(γ(r)−z₀)=r. Its subsequent arclength representation is unit speed. The predictor-defect estimate assumes an exact root and exact unit kernel tangent on the stated convex tube.

During an attempt the previous unit orientation remains the section normal, while the current tangent candidate supplies the predictor. Accepted and attempted counts start at zero; the seed is not an appended step. Zero requested steps return the seed, and continuation budgets cap attempts.

Acceptance requires the explicit contraction certificate on a closed ball contained wholly in the isolating chart neighborhood. Residual tolerance alone is not a root certificate, and termination assumes every invoked callback returns in finite time.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated C¹ square residual and certified residual/Jacobian errors, set β=β̂/(1−β̂εJ), ρ=‖ĝ‖₂+εg, and q=βLR. If β̂εJ<1, q<1, and βρ≤(1−q)R, then G has exactly one zero y* in the closed radius-R ball and ‖y*−y‖₂≤βρ/(1−q).
For rank-n A: R^(n+1)→R^n, a unit kernel vector t, Q=(A restricted to t⊥)⁻¹, and unit τ, B=[A;τᵀ] is invertible exactly when τᵀt≠0. If |τᵀt|≥c>0 and ‖Qu‖₂≤KA‖u‖₂, then ‖B⁻¹‖op≤sqrt(KA²(1+c⁻¹)²+c⁻²).

A C² residual at a rank-n zero has a unique local C² chart normalized by tᵀ(γ(r)−z₀)=r, containing every nearby zero, and a C¹ unit-speed reparameterization. On the stated convex tube with L-Lipschitz DF, the exact tangent predictor has augmented residual at most sqrt(n)Lh²/2.
If τᵀc′(s)≥κ>0 on the supplied two-sided chart interval and d=τᵀ(zp−z₀) satisfies 0≤d≤κr+, exactly one chart parameter in [−r−,r+] satisfies τᵀ(c(s*)−zp)=0.

Under the stated C³, rank-(n−1), nullvector, and nonzero a=wᵀFλ and b=wᵀFxx[v,v] hypotheses, there is a unique local normalized C³ solution curve with x′(0)=v, λ′(0)=0, λ″(0)=−b/a≠0, and a bounded cubic parameter remainder. The full derivative has rank n, and a unit section normal transverse to (v,0) gives an invertible augmented derivative.

The finite-budget procedure generates candidates for previous-normal sections, appends a ball only after the explicit contraction and whole-ball chart checks pass, preserves a certified prefix on failure, and separately finalizes any requested local fold certificate.

concerns.concern: The final Remarks sentence says: “a finite Newton budget alone proves no root exists.” Read literally, this asserts a nonexistence conclusion, contradicting both the theorem and the algorithm's careful inconclusive-status convention. A finite Newton budget alone supplies neither existence nor nonexistence evidence. This appears to be a wording error.

alerts.finding: alg-periodic-orbit-pseudoarclength-continuation states: “The corrector is [[alg-validated-periodic-orbit-corrector]] in section mode, which appends the pseudo-arclength plane and validates the resulting square residual by Krawczyk inclusion,” followed by “Run [[alg-pseudo-arclength-continuation-with-certified-local-corrector]] with these callbacks and its chart, angle, inverse, and finite-budget checks.” The generic supplier does not have a pluggable Krawczyk acceptance branch: its steps 4–5 require thm-augmented-residual-contraction-certificate, including a Euclidean root ball, approximate-Jacobian inverse bound, a Jacobian-Lipschitz constant on that whole ball, and the specific contraction inequalities. The opened periodic corrector instead returns a Krawczyk-certified rational box, terminal partition, residual/Jacobian enclosures and inverse witness; it does not return that ball/Lipschitz/contraction package. A successful Krawczyk box is not automatically a successful instance of the supplier's particular ball test. The composition therefore lacks an explicit adapter or additional input interface establishing the generic acceptance requirements.

seams_checked.note: The local corrector applies the square updated-Jacobian Newton theorem to the augmented residual with the same closed-ball Lipschitz hypothesis, simple-root condition, smaller invariant ball, and KL/2 recurrence. The continuation procedure preserves the finite Newton supplier's residual-stop, singularity, domain and update-budget conventions.

The scalar normal-form theorem specializes the fold supplier with n=1 and v=w=1, retains its normalized curvature sign and local uniqueness, and separately proves the two/one/zero equilibrium count by monotonicity and the intermediate value theorem.

The periodic continuation consumer correctly retains the previous normal, current tangent predictor, rank, angle, chart-offset and conditional-termination qualifications. Its asserted composition substitutes a Krawczyk box corrector without specifying the ball contraction-certificate interface required by the generic supplier; the exact finding is recorded in alerts.
